title: The Second Chebyshev Function ψ ∼ θ: Prime Powers Are Negligible
description: The parent (chebyshev-bounds) bounds the first Chebyshev function θ(x) = Σ_{p≤x} log p and asks (OQ-03) to formalize the second Chebyshev function ψ(x) = Σ_{p^k≤x} log p and show ψ(x) ∼ x ⟺ π(x) ∼ x/log x. Using Mathlib's ψ, θ, and the size estimate |ψ(x) − θ(x)| ≤ 2√x·log x, this entry establishes the first link of that chain rigorously: ψ and θ are asymptotically equivalent. The prime-power correction (ψ − θ counts only p^k with k ≥ 2) is o(x), so ψ(x)/x → 1 ⟺ θ(x)/x → 1. All 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext:
The prime number theorem π(x) ∼ x/log x is most naturally proved via the Chebyshev functions. The first, θ(x) = Σ_{p ≤ x} log p, sums the logarithms of primes; the second, ψ(x) = Σ_{p^k ≤ x} log p = Σ_{n ≤ x} Λ(n) (Λ the von Mangoldt function), also counts prime powers. The three asymptotic statements ψ(x) ∼ x, θ(x) ∼ x, and π(x) ∼ x/log x are all equivalent, and the standard route to PNT is to prove ψ(x) ∼ x and transfer it across these equivalences.

The first equivalence, ψ(x) ∼ x ⟺ θ(x) ∼ x, is elementary: ψ and θ differ only by the contribution of proper prime powers p^k (k ≥ 2), and there are so few of these (≤ √x of them up to x, each contributing ≤ log x) that ψ(x) − θ(x) = O(√x log x) = o(x). Mathlib formalizes both functions and proves precisely the estimate |ψ(x) − θ(x)| ≤ 2√x log x. The parent gallery entry, which bounds θ, raised the formalization of ψ and the equivalence as OQ-03. This entry supplies the ψ ∼ θ equivalence rigorously; the remaining transfer θ ∼ x ⟺ π ∼ x/log x (Abel/partial summation) is the subject of sibling entries.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize that the second Chebyshev function ψ is asymptotically equivalent to the first Chebyshev function θ: prove (ψ(x) − θ(x))/x → 0 and conclude ψ(x)/x → 1 ⟺ θ(x)/x → 1, so that the prime number theorem in the form ψ(x) ∼ x is equivalent to θ(x) ∼ x.
overview.proofStrategy: From Mathlib's |ψ(x) − θ(x)| ≤ 2√x·log x, divide by x to get |(ψ(x) − θ(x))/x| ≤ 2√x·log x/x = 2 log x/√x (using √x/x = 1/√x). The bound 2 log x/√x → 0 because log = o(x^{1/2}) (isLittleO_log_rpow_atTop at r = 1/2) and √x = x^{1/2}; a squeeze (squeeze_zero_norm') then gives (ψ(x) − θ(x))/x → 0. Finally ψ(x)/x = θ(x)/x + (ψ(x) − θ(x))/x, so the limits of ψ/x and θ/x agree (Tendsto.add / Tendsto.sub with the o(x) correction), yielding the equivalence.
keyInsights: ψ and θ differ only by proper prime powers p^k (k ≥ 2), and these are sparse: ψ(x) − θ(x) = O(√x log x), hence o(x).
The o(x) correction is invisible to the leading asymptotic, so ψ(x) ∼ x and θ(x) ∼ x are equivalent — one needs only the size estimate, no deep analysis.
The decay 2 log x/√x → 0 is exactly log = o(x^{1/2}): the logarithm grows slower than any positive power, the single growth fact powering the squeeze.
The equivalence is purely algebraic once the correction vanishes: ψ/x = θ/x + (ψ−θ)/x, so adding a sequence tending to 0 cannot change the limit.
This isolates the easy, fully formalizable link of the PNT equivalence chain (ψ ∼ θ), separating it cleanly from the genuine partial-summation step θ ∼ x ⟺ π ∼ x/log x.
prerequisites: Chebyshev functions ψ, θ and the von Mangoldt function
log = o(x^r) for positive powers, and √x = x^{1/2}
Limit arithmetic (a sequence plus an o(1) term has the same limit)

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) file of 100 lines and 5 theorems establishing that the second Chebyshev function ψ is asymptotically equivalent to the first, θ. Using Mathlib's estimate |ψ(x) − θ(x)| ≤ 2√x·log x and the growth fact log = o(x^{1/2}), it proves (ψ(x) − θ(x))/x → 0 and hence ψ(x)/x → 1 ⟺ θ(x)/x → 1.
conclusion.implications: This answers the ψ ∼ θ half of the parent's OQ-03: the second Chebyshev function carries the same ∼ x content as the first, so the prime number theorem may be proved in whichever form is most convenient. It cleanly isolates the elementary link of the PNT equivalence chain (governed entirely by the sparsity of prime powers) from the genuine partial-summation step θ ∼ x ⟺ π ∼ x/log x pursued in the sibling chebyshev-pnt-bridge entries. The decay lemma log x/√x → 0 and the squeeze pattern are reusable for other o(x) error-term arguments.
openQuestions: Complete the chain: prove θ(x) ∼ x ⟺ π(x) ∼ x/log x via Abel/partial summation, formalizing the transfer between the prime-log sum and the prime-counting function.
Sharpen the correction: formalize the better bound ψ(x) − θ(x) = O(√x) (without the log factor) by a more careful count of prime powers.
